requirements.evidence: All task bullets are covered by the diff or verified by the new tests: app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php:30-51 has the config guard/no-op, JSON POST with a 5s timeout, and non-2xx plus transport error logging; :59-65 builds title/message/key=value lines and applies the 1800-character mb_substr truncation; :74-81 redacts sensitive keys, Bearer values and nested arrays recursively; :98-102 scrubs the webhook URL before logging. config/logging.php:57 changes the stack default to daily and :76-82 adds the audit daily/info/90 channel; tests/Feature/LoggingConfigTest.php:5-9 asserts the daily driver/path/14, :11-14 the audit path/days/level and :17-20 the stack/no-discord contract. config/services.php:31-33 reads DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL; .env.example:19-27 and phpunit.xml:29 add the required keys; docs/ops/logging.md:8-18 documents the three lanes and decision guide.

conventions.evidence: The change ships Pest tests for the new behavior (tests/Feature/LoggingConfigTest.php, tests/Feature/Ops/DiscordOpsAlertTest.php), adds docs/ops/logging.md (already referenced from conventions.md:54), updates CHANGELOG.md:12,19, and matches sibling config style in config/logging.php. No migrations, Livewire components, policies or domain Actions are involved, so no other project convention applies; PHPDoc is present on the public send() method.

security.evidence: Redaction constants at app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php:23-25 and the recursive redaction at :74-81 cover every listed sensitive key, Bearer strings and nested arrays; failure logs at :44 and :47-50 contain only the status code, exception class and the scrubbed message; :98-102 removes both the exact configured URL and any /api/webhooks/ URL from exception text. No required redaction or URL scrub is omitted, and there is no user-authorization surface in this ops service.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/Ops/DiscordOpsAlertTest.php:27-34 covers the null/empty no-op, :36-45 the POST/JSON/format contract, :47-53 the 1800-character multibyte truncation, :55-78 key/Bearer/nested redaction, :80-91 non-2xx logging and :93-103 transport exceptions; tests/Feature/LoggingConfigTest.php:5-20 covers daily/audit/stack/no-discord config. Gaps: the audit-write assertion at :22-25 is non-observable, and the config assertions at :6-14 only check defaults while phpunit.xml:29 pins only LOG_STACK.

simplicity.evidence: app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php:30-102 is a lean 104-line class with four small private helpers and constants; it reuses Laravel's Http, Log and config facilities and introduces no speculative abstraction, duplication or dead code.

readability.evidence: Clear constant and method names (MAX_LENGTH, TIMEOUT_SECONDS, SENSITIVE_KEY; format/redact/stringify/scrub), short PHPDoc, and a linear flow in app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php:17-102; the tests read as behavior specs (tests/Feature/Ops/DiscordOpsAlertTest.php:27-103).

scope.evidence: The diff touches only task-related files: the notifier, config/logging.php, config/services.php, .env.example, phpunit.xml, docs/ops/logging.md, CHANGELOG.md and tests; there are no unrelated refactors, features or edits.

issues.explanation: The audit-write test calls Log::channel('audit')->info(...) but then only asserts the channel object is non-null, so it would still pass if the entry were silently filtered or dropped; assert the write with Log::fake()/Log::spy() or inspect the log file.

The config tests assert env-derived defaults but phpunit.xml:29 pins only LOG_STACK, so a developer .env with a different LOG_DAILY_DAYS, LOG_AUDIT_LEVEL or LOG_AUDIT_DAYS breaks the suite, and no test proves those env keys are actually wired.

docs/ops/logging.md:37-38 says the test environment leaves DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL empty, but phpunit.xml does not pin it; add <env name="DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL" value=""/> so a local .env with a real webhook can never be used by the suite.

review.summary: The change implements the three logging lanes: a focused App\Ops\DiscordOpsAlert with config-driven no-op, JSON POST, 1800-character truncation, recursive redaction and URL-scrubbed soft-fail logging, plus the daily/audit channel config, stack default, env keys, phpunit pin, docs and CHANGELOG. Requirements, security, conventions and scope are met; the remaining concerns are test robustness (the audit-write assertion is not observable, the config assertions still depend on a local .env and skip the new env overrides) and the missing DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL test pin, so I would approve after those small test improvements.
